## Hidden Numbers: An Exploration of Factors that Influence Human Trafficking Detection and Government Response in Europe {.project-title}
### Georgetown University • DSAN 5000 (Data Science & Analytics) {.project-location}

<p style="font-size: 1rem; font-weight: normal; line-height: 1.5;">In this project, I conducted extensive background research and assembled a comprehensive dataset on human trafficking by collecting, cleaning, and standardizing indicators from multiple reliable sources. The goal was to better understand which variables explain government responses to this rapidly growing and complex form of underground crime. I performed advanced exploratory data analysis and applied a range of supervised (regression and classification) and unsupervised machine learning techniques to model and evaluate these factors. This work contributes a novel data-driven framework for studying human trafficking and assessing related policy efforts.</p>
:::

## Data vs. Dogma: Maternal Wellness Conditions and Abortion Policy per State{.project-title}
### Georgetown University • DSAN 5100 (Probabilistic Modeling & Statistical Computing) {.project-location}

<p style="font-size: 1rem; font-weight: normal; line-height: 1.5;">This project explores how state-level maternal, infant, and overall health outcomes *prior* to the Dobbs decision relate to the abortion policies states implemented the ruling. My group and I conducted extensive background research and built a unified dataset by gathering, cleaning, and standardizing data from a wide range of reliable sources. Using R, we performed advanced exploratory analysis, statistical testing, and visualizations to examine these relationships. The goal was to provide data-driven insights that can inform more transparent and evidence-based reproductive health policymaking.</p>
:::
